quadrant.title: Views × Intent quadrant
quadrant.subtitle: Every published post on two independent axes: how far it traveled compared with its account's median (×{multiplier} to count as high) and how much of its audience saved it ({saveRate} to count as high). Under {minViews} views the save rate is not readable — the post does not move up. Scores recomputed by the nightly sync.
quadrant.empty: No post can be plotted for this period.

tooltip.pending: Pending — under {hours} h, too early to judge.

info.title: This chart answers one question: for each post, where is the problem? A post can fail in two different ways: TikTok did not distribute it (a hook problem), or it was seen but nobody showed any interest in the product (a product-intro problem). These two failures are fixed in opposite ways — this chart separates them so you don't fix the wrong thing.
info.axisX: Did TikTok push this post? Measured against the account's median over {windowDays} days: a post is 'high' if it did at least ×{multiplier} the median of ITS OWN account. It is relative: 10,000 views is a burst on a small account and an ordinary day on a big one.
info.axisY: Did viewers show product interest? Measured by the save rate (saves ÷ views), threshold at {saveRate}. A save = 'I'm keeping this for later' — it is the signal most correlated with sales in our history. Likes measure emotion, saves measure intent.
info.scale: Distributed AND saved: the hook lands and the product appeals. Action: run this format/hook again, it is a proven winner.
info.intent_faible: TikTok distributed it but nobody saves: people watch without taking an interest in the product. The hook is good — leave it alone. The problem is the bridge to the product: mentioned too late, unclear, or missing. Action: tighten the product intro.
info.distribution_faible: Few views but a high save rate: the small audience reached is strongly interested in the product. The angle is good — keep it. It is the hook that did not land hard enough for TikTok to push. Action: change the hook, keep the angle.
info.archiver: Neither distribution nor interest. One failed run can be bad luck (TikTok distribution is a lottery): archive after 2 failed runs, not 1.
info.pending: A post under {hours}h old is not classified: its views are still climbing, and classifying it now would give a false verdict. Classification settles at {hours}h.
info.breakout: This post was published within {windowHours}h of a breakout (≥{minViews}) from the same account. Its numbers are probably inflated by the breakout's redistribution — read its classification with caution, it is not necessarily its own performance.
info.autre: Post never marked warmup or promo in Jarvia. Qualify it so that filters and readings are accurate.

warmupGuide.igPhasesTitle: Warm-up in phases (D1 → D14) — no posting
warmupGuide.youtubeIntro: YouTube is far more permissive. The account is tied to your existing Google account, so there's less suspicion.
commonRules: **A dedicated email per account**, no `+` aliases
**Native mobile app only** during the warm-up and your first 10 posts (no web, no API/scheduler)
**No VPN**, strict geo-consistency (device + SIM + IP in the same country)
**Keep the profile minimal for the first few days**: no sales bio, no aggressive external link
Engage **exclusively inside your target niche** from day 1

tiktokBlocks.subtitle: Warm-up phase (D1 → D7) — no posting
items: **Daily searches with YOUR keywords** in the search bar
20–30 min/day scrolling the FYP inside your niche
Full watch time on videos in your niche (no fast scrolling)
10–20 likes/day, 2–3 genuine comments (not "🔥")
5–10 follows/day max, on accounts in your niche
Fill in your bio and profile picture during this phase

tiktokBlocks.subtitle: First post — D8 (the day after the warm-up)
items: **No posting before D8**: the warm-up runs a full 7 days

tiktokBlocks.subtitle: Ramping up (after the first post)
items: 1 post/day for 7–10 days before increasing the pace

igSetup.subtitle: Setup
items: Create the account → leave the profile empty at first
Fill in bio + profile picture + 1 highlight during the warm-up

igPhases.subtitle: D1 to D3 — pure observation
items: **Daily searches with YOUR keywords**
15–20 min scrolling the feed + Stories
5–10 likes/day
**Zero follows, zero comments**

igPhases.subtitle: D4 to D10 — light engagement
items: Daily searches with your keywords
5–10 follows/day in your niche
15–20 likes/day
2–3 genuine comments
Like and **save** Reels from your niche

igPhases.subtitle: D11 to D14 — normal activity
items: 15–25 likes/day, 5–10 comments
Saves on relevant posts (strong signal)
First Stories possible from D14–15

igPremier.subtitle: First Reel — D15 (the day after the warm-up)
items: **No Reel before D15**: the warm-up runs a full 14 days

igPremier.subtitle: Ramping up (after the first Reel)
items: Build up gradually toward normal activity

youtubeBlocks.subtitle: Channel setup
items: Banner, profile picture, channel description, full About page
Create 1 playlist (even an empty one)
Link your social accounts in the description

youtubeBlocks.subtitle: Warm-up phase (D1 → D7) — no posting
items: **Daily searches with YOUR keywords**
Watch 5–10 Shorts/day in your niche
1–2 long videos/day in your niche (a strong signal for YT)
Likes + 2–3 genuine comments
10–20 subscriptions to relevant channels

youtubeBlocks.subtitle: First Short — D8 (the day after the warm-up)
items: **No Short before D8**: the warm-up runs a full 7 days
After that, 1 Short/day, ideally at the same time

cleanSignals.signal: Views on the first post at H+6
Your own feed has become niche

failedSignals: Views stuck at 0–50, or exactly 200 over and over
FYP / Reels feed / Shorts feed traffic = 0% in Analytics
Posts visible only to your existing followers
A drop of 70%+ against the 28-day average
resetSteps: **Stop posting immediately** (this is the one that matters)
Delete videos under 50 views (a permanent negative signal)
Take an **active** 5–7 day break: scroll your niche 20–30 min/day, post nothing
Repost ONE video and watch what happens
Still 0 views → drop the account and create a fresh one

dontBlocks.subtitle: During the warm-up
items: Posting before the warm-up is over
Following 50+ accounts on day one
Generic comments ("nice", "🔥") in bulk
Engaging outside your niche (it confuses the algorithm about your classification)
Changing your bio or profile picture every day
Switching between VPNs / different IPs

dontBlocks.subtitle: At post-warm-up launch
items: Dropping 3 videos at once
Using a scheduler/API for your first 10 posts
Shady or banned hashtags (always check them in the search bar)
Engagement bait ("like if you agree", "follow for part 2") — an instant flag in 2026
Copyrighted music on a business account
Cross-posting the **same video file** to several accounts (file fingerprinting is detected)

dontBlocks.subtitle: Ongoing
items: Stopping scrolling the platform once you're in posting mode (the algorithm tracks your consumption too)
Spam-posting after a hit (going from 1/day to 10/day is a flag)
Switching between accounts every 10 minutes
